user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration Checklist (Night Before)

- [ ] Notify all team members — **freeze SVN commits** during migration
- [ ] Confirm Git hosting destination (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted)
- [ ] Ensure tools are installed: `git`, `git-svn`, `svn`
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

---

## Phase 1 — Preparation (9:00–10:00 AM)

### 1.1 Audit the SVN Repo
```bash
# Check repo size and revision count
svn info https://your-svn-repo/url

# List authors (you'll need to map them)
svn log --quiet https://your-svn-repo/url | \
  grep "^r" | awk '{print $3}' | sort -u
```

### 1.2 Create Authors Mapping File
```bash
# authors.txt — maps SVN usernames to Git identities
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
(no author) = Unknown <unknown@company.com>
```

### 1.3 Identify Repo Layout
| Layout Type | Flag to Use |
|---|---|
| Standard (`trunk/branches/tags`) | `--stdlayout` |
| Custom layout | `--trunk=`, `--branches=`, `--tags=` |

---

## Phase 2 — Clone SVN → Git (10:00 AM–12:00 PM)

### 2.1 Run `git svn clone`
```bash
# Standard layout
git svn clone https://your-svn-repo/url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors.txt \
  my-project

cd my-project
```

> ⏱️ **Time estimate:** ~1 min per 1,000 revisions. Small repos are usually fast.

### 2.2 Verify the Clone
```bash
git log --oneline -20        # Check commit history
git branch -a                # Check branches
git tag                      # Check tags
```

---

## Phase 3 — Clean Up the Git Repo (12:00–1:00 PM)

### 3.1 Convert SVN Branches & Tags to Git Natives
```bash
# Convert remote SVN branches to local Git branches
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v "tags/" | grep -v trunk); do
  git branch "${branch##*/}" "$branch"
done

# Convert SVN tags to real Git tags
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep "tags/"); do
  git tag "${tag##*/tags/}" "$tag"
  git branch -d -r "$tag"
done
```

### 3.2 Remove SVN Tracking Refs
```bash
git branch -d -r trunk
# Remove any remaining remote refs
git config --remove-section svn-remote.svn
rm -rf .git/svn
```

### 3.3 Clean Up `.gitignore`
```bash
# Convert svn:ignore properties to .gitignore
git svn show-ignore > .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Add .gitignore from SVN ignore properties"
```

---

## Phase 4 — Push to Remote Git Host (1:00–2:00 PM)

### 4.1 Create Empty Repo on Git Host
- Create a **bare, empty** repo (no README, no license auto-init)

### 4.2 Push Everything
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/your-org/my-project.git

# Push all branches
git push origin --all

# Push all tags
git push origin --tags
```

### 4.3 Set Default Branch
```bash
git checkout main 2>/dev/null || git checkout -b main origin/trunk
git push origin main
# Set main as default on your Git host UI
```

---

## Phase 5 — Validation (2:00–3:00 PM)

### Verification Checklist
- [ ] Commit count matches SVN revision count (approximately)
- [ ] All branches are present
- [ ] All tags are present
- [ ] Author names/emails are correct
- [ ] `.gitignore` is working
- [ ] Build/CI pipeline runs successfully on new repo
- [ ] README and key files are intact

```bash
# Quick sanity checks
git log --oneline | wc -l      # Commit count
git branch -a                  # All branches
git tag | wc -l                # Tag count
```

---

## Phase 6 — Team Onboarding (3:00–5:00 PM)

### 6.1 Each Developer Clones Fresh
```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/my-project.git
cd my-project
```

### 6.2 Share a Quick-Reference Cheat Sheet

| SVN Command | Git Equivalent |
|---|---|
| `svn update` | `git pull` |
| `svn commit` | `git add . && git commit && git push` |
| `svn checkout` | `git clone` |
| `svn revert` | `git checkout -- <file>` |
| `svn log` | `git log` |
| `svn diff` | `git diff` |
| `svn branch` | `git checkout -b` |

### 6.3 Disable / Archive SVN Repo
- Set SVN repo to **read-only**
- Post a notice pointing to the new Git URL
- Archive after a 2-week safety window

---

## Risk & Rollback Plan

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Author mapping incomplete | Re-run with updated `authors.txt` |
| History looks wrong | Keep SVN read-only as reference |
| Large binary files | Consider Git LFS before pushing |
| CI/CD breaks | Update pipeline config same day |

---

## End-of-Day Summary

```
✅ SVN repo cloned with full history
✅ Branches and tags converted
✅ Pushed to remote Git host
✅ Team cloned and verified
✅ SVN set to read-only
✅ CI/CD updated and passing
```

> **Total time: ~6–8 hours** for a small repo with a small team.

Based on the migration plan above, the top 3 risks are:

---

### 1. 🔴 Incomplete Author Mapping
**What goes wrong:** Any SVN username missing from `authors.txt` causes `git svn clone` to **halt mid-migration**, potentially mid-way through thousands of revisions.

**Impact:** Wasted time, partial clone, must restart.

**Mitigation:**
- Audit *all* authors before starting (Phase 1.1)
- Add a catch-all fallback in `authors.txt`:
  ```
  (no author) = Unknown <unknown@company.com>
  ```

---

### 2. 🔴 CI/CD Pipeline Breaks
**What goes wrong:** Pipelines hardcoded to the SVN URL, SVN-specific commands (`svn checkout`), or old branch naming conventions **stop working immediately** after cutover.

**Impact:** Broken builds block the whole team on day one.

**Mitigation:**
- Audit pipeline configs *before* migration day
- Test CI/CD against the new Git repo in Phase 5 before onboarding the team

---

### 3. 🟡 Corrupt or Missing History for Branches & Tags
**What goes wrong:** Non-standard SVN layouts or messy branch histories can cause branches/tags to be **missing, misnamed, or have broken history** after conversion.

**Impact:** Loss of traceability; developers lose access to historical context.

**Mitigation:**
- Verify branch/tag counts match before pushing (Phase 5)
- Keep SVN **read-only** as a reference for at least 2 weeks

---

> **Bottom line:** Author mapping and CI/CD are the most likely to cause same-day failures. History corruption is less likely but the hardest to fix after the fact.

## Top 3 Risk Checklist

### 1. Author Mapping
- [ ] Extract all SVN authors before migration day
- [ ] Verify every author has an entry in `authors.txt`
- [ ] Add a catch-all fallback entry

### 2. CI/CD Pipeline
- [ ] Audit pipeline configs for SVN-specific URLs/commands
- [ ] Update configs to point to new Git repo
- [ ] Run a test build before team onboarding

### 3. Branch & Tag History
- [ ] Confirm branch/tag counts match SVN after clone
- [ ] Spot-check commit history on key branches
- [ ] Keep SVN read-only for 2 weeks as a fallback

## Rollback Option

**Keep SVN read-only as a live fallback.**

If the migration fails or critical history is found to be missing or corrupt, revert the team back to the SVN repo by re-enabling write access.

> **Key requirement:** The SVN commit freeze must stay in place for this to work — if no one has committed to Git yet, SVN remains a clean and exact fallback with zero data loss.

## Prerequisite

**Freeze all SVN commits before migration begins.**

No new commits should be made to SVN during the migration. If developers continue committing, the Git clone will be out of sync and the rollback option is compromised.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
## Fastest Validation Step

**Compare commit counts between SVN and Git.**

```bash
# SVN revision count
svn info https://your-svn-repo/url | grep "Last Changed Rev"

# Git commit count
git log --oneline | wc -l
```

> Takes less than 30 seconds and immediately tells you if history is missing.
**9 AM** Prep → **10 AM** Clone → **12 PM** Clean up → **1 PM** Push → **2 PM** Validate → **3 PM** Onboard → **5 PM** Done.

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
## Two Tools

1. **`git svn`** — Built-in Git command that clones SVN history, branches, and tags into a local Git repository.

2. **`svn2git`** — A Ruby wrapper around `git svn` that automates author mapping and branch/tag conversion, reducing manual cleanup steps.

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text:
## Final Cutover Approval

**The project or team lead** should approve the final cutover, as they are accountable for confirming that:
- All team members are notified
- Validation checks have passed
- CI/CD is working on the new repo

> No cutover should proceed without their explicit sign-off.

## Communication Tip

**Send a single clear message to the whole team before migration starts**, stating the SVN freeze time, the expected Git URL, and who to contact if something goes wrong.

## Final Recap

| # | Step | Key Point |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Prep | Freeze SVN, map all authors |
| 2 | Clone | Use `git svn` or `svn2git` |
| 3 | Clean Up | Convert branches, tags, `.gitignore` |
| 4 | Push | Push all branches and tags to Git host |
| 5 | Validate | Compare commit counts as fastest check |
| 6 | Onboard | Team clones fresh, share cheat sheet |
| 7 | Cutover | Team lead approves, SVN set to read-only |

**Top 3 Risks:** Author mapping, CI/CD pipeline, branch/tag history.

**Rollback:** Keep SVN read-only for 2 weeks.

**Timeline:** 9 AM – 5 PM, one day.

> A small repo with good preparation should migrate cleanly in a single working day with minimal disruption.

## Final Recap

- Freeze SVN before starting
- Map all authors in advance
- Use `git svn` or `svn2git`
- Convert branches and tags
- Push all branches and tags
- Compare commit counts to validate
- Team lead approves cutover
- Keep SVN read-only for 2 weeks
- Done in one day, 9 AM – 5 PM
